trust_decision.summary: Whether DOCTYPE / external entities in the XML strings passed to isXmlEqualTo are processed is decided by the DocumentBuilderFactory features set in XmlStringPrettyFormatter.documentBuilderFactory(); at the pinned commit these hardening features are ALREADY applied (the pinned commit is the security merge itself).

landing_point.why: Summary names the isXmlEqualTo assertion; it delegates to Strings.assertXmlEqualsTo, which calls xmlPrettyFormat, the only XML parser in the repo.

fix_sites.entry_point: none (listed fix commit only adds @Deprecated + javadoc to XmlStringPrettyFormatter; no behavioural change)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered route exists; the only XML parser in the tree is already hardened at the pinned commit.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Pretty-format/compare of ordinary XML incl. preserving the <?xml declaration must keep working; disallowing DOCTYPE already rejects all DTD-bearing documents

O6_input_shapes: parameter entity in internal DTD subset

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second XML comparison path (e.g. a Path/InputStream XML assertion or an XPath/attribute-ignoring comparator) building its own DocumentBuilderFactory/TransformerFactory without the hardening map
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: XML assertions are a natural feature extension and the hardening map is a private static in XmlStringPrettyFormatter, so a new parser would not inherit it; still a WHERE-type sibling only

O9_family: XXE (CWE-611) in a test-assertion library XML parser

O10_build.toolchain: Maven (multi-module, JDK 17+ for text blocks in tests)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set disallow-doctype-decl / FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING on the DocumentBuilderFactory in XmlStringPrettyFormatter (which is the real fix, and already present at the pinned commit).

out_of_scope_notes: Pinned commit 77081dc5e ('Merge commit from fork') already contains the XXE hardening and XXE tests; the listed fix commit 85ca7eb only deprecates the class, so the pinned tree is not vulnerable.

documentBuilderFactory() swallows ParserConfigurationException per feature (XmlStringPrettyFormatter.java:97-101), so a non-Xerces JAXP provider rejecting a feature would silently drop it; not pursued.
